boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Louisiana Tech University
boards.description: Ten currently source-verified, under-21-safe food destinations in Ruston with service at midnight or later.

cards.title: Whataburger on North Service Road East
cards.subtitle: 801 N Service Rd E, Ruston
cards.notes: Use the 24-hour dine-in or drive-thru option when you need a food stop; confirm holiday changes before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour Ruston Whataburger location with dine-in and drive-thru service.
cards.evidence_claim: Whataburger lists its 801 N Service Rd E, Ruston location as 24-hour for dine-in and drive-thru every day.
cards.source_title: Whataburger — 801 N Service Rd E, Ruston
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists dine-in and drive-thru as 24 hours daily; holiday hours may differ.

cards.title: Taco Bell on West California Avenue
cards.subtitle: 301 W California Ave, Ruston
cards.notes: Choose the drive-thru for a late food pickup; the official listing shows later closing on Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A Ruston Taco Bell with drive-thru service until 1 a.m. most nights and 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru hours until 1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday at 301 W California Ave.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 301 W California Ave, Ruston
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru until 1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday; dine-in hours differ.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Farmerville Highway
cards.subtitle: 2103 Farmerville Hwy, Ruston
cards.notes: Plan for the drive-thru if you are out late; check the day-specific closing time before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A second Ruston Taco Bell with nightly late drive-thru availability.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru hours until 1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday at 2103 Farmerville Hwy.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru until 1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday; dine-in hours differ.

cards.title: Wendy’s on North Trenton Street
cards.subtitle: 1400 North Trenton St, Ruston
cards.notes: This is a food-only late option with restaurant and drive-thru service listed through 1 a.m.; verify changes on holidays.
cards.short_summary: A Ruston Wendy’s with restaurant and drive-thru hours through 1 a.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy's lists restaurant and drive-thru hours of 6:30 a.m.–1 a.m. daily at 1400 North Trenton St.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists both restaurant and drive-thru open until 1 a.m. every day.

cards.title: Pizza Hut on Tech Drive
cards.subtitle: 975 Tech Dr, Ruston
cards.notes: Use carryout or delivery for a late meal; the official location page shows midnight closing on Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A Tech Drive pizza option with midnight Friday–Saturday restaurant hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Hut lists restaurant hours until midnight Friday and Saturday at 975 Tech Dr in Ruston.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists restaurant hours until 11 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and midnight Friday–Saturday; delivery hours may vary.

cards.title: Subway on Tech Drive
cards.subtitle: 1105 Tech Drive, Ruston
cards.notes: For a late sandwich stop, use the Friday or Saturday midnight window and confirm the location’s current service options first.
cards.short_summary: A Tech Drive Subway listed open until midnight on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Subway lists its 1105 Tech Drive location open until midnight on Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists 8 a.m.–11 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and 8 a.m.–midnight Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Subway at U-Pak It C-Store/Exxon Gas
cards.subtitle: 110 Woodward Ave, Ruston
cards.notes: Use this named Subway location for an around-the-clock food stop; order or pick up through the services shown on its location page.
cards.short_summary: A Subway inside the U-Pak It C-Store/Exxon Gas listed open 24 hours every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Subway lists the U-Pak It C-Store/Exxon Gas location at 110 Woodward Ave as open 24 hours daily.
cards.source_title: Subway — U-Pak It C-Store/Exxon Gas, Ruston
cards.access_notes: Official page lists the store as open 24 hours Monday–Sunday.

cards.title: Waffle House on Farmerville Highway
cards.subtitle: 1508 Farmerville Hwy, Ruston
cards.notes: Visit this all-hours diner location for a seated meal; use the destination listing to confirm the address before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A Farmerville Highway Waffle House identified by Ruston’s official tourism organization as open 24 hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Experience Ruston identifies Waffle House at 1508 Farmerville Hwy and states that Waffle House is open 24 hours a day.
cards.source_title: Experience Ruston — Waffle House, Farmerville Hwy
cards.access_notes: Ruston’s tourism listing states Waffle House is open 24 hours a day and gives this location’s address.

cards.title: Waffle House on Cooktown Road
cards.subtitle: 1121 Cooktown Rd, Ruston
cards.notes: Use the second named Ruston Waffle House location when you need a meal after conventional dinner hours; confirm details before travel.
cards.short_summary: A second Ruston Waffle House location included in the tourism listing’s 24-hour dining information.
cards.evidence_claim: Experience Ruston lists 1121 Cooktown Rd as a second Ruston Waffle House location and states Waffle House is open 24 hours a day.
cards.source_title: Experience Ruston — Waffle House, Farmerville Hwy
cards.access_notes: Ruston’s tourism listing states Waffle House is open 24 hours a day and names the Cooktown Road location.

cards.title: Huddle House on North Service Road East
cards.subtitle: 501 N Service Rd E, Ruston
cards.notes: Use this named diner for a food stop at any hour; check the restaurant’s current location page before relying on the schedule.
cards.short_summary: A North Service Road East diner listed as open 24 hours in Ruston.
cards.evidence_claim: Huddle House’s Ruston location page is identified for 501 N Service Rd E; the Ruston restaurant listing reports daily 24-hour hours for that location.
cards.source_title: Huddle House — 501 N Service Rd E, Ruston
cards.access_notes: The official Huddle House location URL identifies 501 N Service Rd E; current web-indexed location information reports 24-hour daily service. Confirm directly before travel.

warnings: Late hours can change for holidays, staffing, or service mode; confirm the cited location page before leaving.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Louisiana Tech spaces for studying, low-key recreation, art, and campus landmarks, supported by current University sources.

cards.title: Pause at Lady of the Mist
cards.subtitle: Quadrangle landmark
cards.notes: Use the fountain as a recognizable meeting point before crossing the quadrangle; take a moment to read the campus’s account of its symbolism.
cards.short_summary: A fountain sculpture in the quadrangle with a documented connection to Louisiana Tech’s campus identity.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech identifies Lady of the Mist as a beloved campus landmark and says it stands in a fountain in the quadrangle.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; follow posted campus access and parking rules.

cards.entity_name: Prescott Memorial Library Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Claim a Group Study Room
cards.subtitle: Prescott Memorial Library
cards.notes: Bring your Tech ID and check at Circulation when your group needs a focused work session; rooms serve groups of three to eight and are first-come.
cards.short_summary: Four nonreservable group rooms for small academic work sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Prescott Memorial Library has four group study rooms for groups of three to eight; Tech students sign in and leave a valid Tech ID at Circulation.
cards.access_notes: For Tech students; rooms cannot be reserved and are not for regularly scheduled meetings or classes.

cards.title: Reset in the Sensory Space
cards.subtitle: Main floor, Prescott Memorial Library
cards.notes: Use the main-floor room for a quiet reset, study break, or individual work; its adjustable lighting and calming tools support a lower-stimulation visit.
cards.short_summary: A student wellness room with calming accessories, privacy seating, and charging outlets.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sensory Space is on Prescott Memorial Library’s main floor and is open to all Louisiana Tech students for relaxation, well-being, work, and study.
cards.source_title: New Sensory Space opens in Prescott Memorial Library
cards.access_notes: Open to Louisiana Tech students; observe room guidelines and library policies.

cards.title: See What Is Hanging at the Galleries
cards.subtitle: F. Jay Taylor Visual Arts Center
cards.notes: Stop in between classes to view the current work, then check the gallery page for reception timing if an opening is listed for that exhibition.
cards.short_summary: Two School of Design galleries showing work across media in the Visual Arts Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech’s School of Design operates two gallery spaces in the F. Jay Taylor Visual Arts Center; they are free and open to the public Monday through Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; later opening-reception hours are listed by exhibition.

cards.title: Walk the Trail at Hideaway Park
cards.subtitle: Campus recreation park
cards.notes: Plan a daylight walk with a friend, or bring a disc for the marked course; pavilions, the trail, and the lake make this an outdoor change of pace.
cards.short_summary: A campus park with a walking trail, pavilions, lake, and 18-hole disc golf course.
cards.evidence_claim: Hideaway Park is open daily during daylight hours and includes a running/walking trail, pavilions, an 18-hole frisbee golf course, and a seven-acre lake.
cards.access_notes: Open every day during daylight hours; use the established trail and course.

cards.entity_name: Lambright Sports & Wellness Center Bowling Alley
cards.title: Roll a Game at Lambright
cards.subtitle: Lambright Sports & Wellness Center
cards.notes: Bring a valid Tech ID for a casual group game on one of the six lanes; balls, tables, and automatic scoring are available in the alley.
cards.short_summary: A six-lane campus bowling alley inside Lambright.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lambright bowling alley has six lanes and is free for Louisiana Tech students with a valid student ID.
cards.access_notes: Open to currently enrolled students and current Lambright members; a valid student ID is required for free student use.

cards.entity_name: Lambright Sports & Wellness Center Aquatics Facility
cards.title: Use the Aquatics Facility
cards.subtitle: Lambright Sports & Wellness Center
cards.notes: Check the facility schedule before going, then choose the indoor pool for exercise or the seasonal outdoor leisure pool when it is operating.
cards.short_summary: Indoor competition/exercise lanes plus a seasonal outdoor leisure pool.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lambright Aquatics Facility has an indoor eight-lane, 25-yard pool for competition and exercise and an outdoor leisure pool open from late spring to early fall.
cards.access_notes: Students and members are welcomed; pool availability can change for weather and special events.

cards.title: Train in the Talton Fitness Room
cards.subtitle: Downstairs at Lambright
cards.notes: Use the downstairs room for a self-directed workout with racks, free weights, machines, and cardio equipment; ask the desk about available fitness help.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated Lambright fitness room with strength and cardio equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: The Billy Jack Talton Fitness Room is downstairs at Lambright and includes power racks, free weights, machine weights, and cardio equipment.
cards.access_notes: A valid student or member ID is required for Lambright entry; follow facility attire and equipment policies.

cards.entity_name: Lambright Sports & Wellness Center Rock Wall
cards.title: Try the Lambright Rock Wall
cards.subtitle: Lambright Sports & Wellness Center
cards.notes: Check in during climbing hours and follow staff direction before using the wall; the setup includes two manual belays and six auto-belays.
cards.short_summary: A 29.5-foot indoor climbing wall with manual and automatic belays.
cards.evidence_claim: Lambright’s rock wall is 29.5 feet tall and has two manual belays and six auto-belays.
cards.access_notes: Monday–Friday, 4–8 p.m.; consult the current recreation schedule for changes.

cards.title: Meet at Centennial Plaza
cards.subtitle: Main campus landmark
cards.notes: Use the named plaza and tower as a clear rendezvous point while crossing campus, then consult the current campus map to orient your next stop.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed plaza and tower on Louisiana Tech’s main campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech’s updated July 2025 campus map lists Centennial Plaza/Centennial Tower as a named main-campus destination.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus destination; follow posted campus access and parking rules.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission, no-purchase ways to spend time on campus or in Ruston, using public-access and no-charge information from Louisiana Tech and the City of Ruston.

cards.title: See the School of Design Galleries
cards.subtitle: Jay Taylor Visual Arts Center, 1 Mayfield Ave.
cards.notes: Drop into the School of Design’s two gallery spaces and talk through the work together; weekday gallery access is free and open to the public.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission campus art stop with rotating contemporary work.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech lists its School of Design Galleries as free and open to the public, Monday through Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.
cards.source_title: Louisiana Tech School of Design Art Galleries
cards.access_notes: Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; free and open to the public. Check the gallery page before visiting for reception exceptions.

cards.entity_name: Browse Federal Depository documents at Prescott Memorial Library
cards.title: Browse federal documents together
cards.subtitle: Prescott Memorial Library, 201 Mayfield Ave.
cards.notes: Choose a topic and explore the federal document collection side by side; materials are available for free public use during library hours.
cards.short_summary: A research-minded hang among a large federal documents collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Prescott Memorial Library is open to the public and welcomes use of its federal government document collections; its policies state free public access.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; use collections during library open hours. Borrowing has separate ID or courtesy-card requirements.

cards.entity_name: Explore Louisiana state documents at Prescott Memorial Library
cards.title: Explore Louisiana documents
cards.subtitle: Prescott Memorial Library, 201 Mayfield Ave.
cards.notes: Compare old and current state publications or maps at the library’s depository shelves; public access to state documents is free during open hours.
cards.short_summary: A free, locally grounded browse through Louisiana government publications.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech’s Government Documents policy says state depository materials may be accessed by any member of the public during library open hours and are provided free for use.
cards.access_notes: State documents are on the library’s second floor; access them during library open hours. Copying may carry a fee.

cards.entity_name: Use Prescott Memorial Library guest computers
cards.title: Settle in at a guest computer
cards.subtitle: Prescott Memorial Library, 201 Mayfield Ave.
cards.notes: Meet up for a low-key research session using the library’s designated guest computers, which provide free public internet access during open hours.
cards.short_summary: A free indoor option for browsing, planning, or shared research.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech states that designated guest computers on Prescott Memorial Library’s second floor offer free public internet access.
cards.access_notes: Guest computers are on the second floor and available during library open hours; they are intended for library catalog and government-publication access.

cards.title: Scan a shared project
cards.subtitle: Prescott Memorial Library, 201 Mayfield Ave.
cards.notes: Bring notes, clippings, or a permitted document and digitize it together; the library specifically identifies its scanners as free to use.
cards.short_summary: A practical no-cost stop for preserving or sharing paper materials.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech’s visitor information states that Prescott Memorial Library scanners are free to use.
cards.source_title: Louisiana Tech Prescott Memorial Library Visitors and Alumni
cards.access_notes: Scanners are free; printing is restricted to active Louisiana Tech community members and photocopies cost 10¢ per page.

cards.title: Catch a Science Seminar
cards.subtitle: Louisiana Tech campus; select Thursdays
cards.notes: Check the seminar schedule, then bring a friend for a science or engineering talk and post-talk conversation; the series is free and public.
cards.short_summary: A campus lecture series spanning science, engineering, and related topics.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech says its Science Seminars occur on select Thursdays in fall, winter, and spring and are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Louisiana Tech College of Engineering & Science Outreach and Seminars
cards.access_notes: Held on select Thursdays during fall, winter, and spring quarters; confirm the current seminar location and date before going.

cards.title: Meet at R. L. Cook Park
cards.subtitle: Ruston city park
cards.notes: Use the open park area for a picnic blanket, conversation, or an easy walk; the city keeps adjoining park areas open to the public.
cards.short_summary: A named Ruston park for an unstructured outdoor meet-up.
cards.evidence_claim: Ruston Parks and Recreation lists R. L. Cook Park and states that adjoining city-park areas remain open and available to the public at all times.
cards.source_title: City of Ruston Parks and Recreation Reservations
cards.access_notes: Use unreserved adjoining park areas; pavilion reservations are optional and separately priced.

cards.title: Take a lap at Duncan Park
cards.subtitle: Ruston city park
cards.notes: Pick a meeting point and walk or sit in the open park area; no purchase or admission is required when you are not reserving a pavilion.
cards.short_summary: A public Ruston green space suited to a simple walk-and-talk.
cards.evidence_claim: Ruston Parks and Recreation lists Duncan Park and says adjoining city-park areas remain open and available to the public at all times.
cards.source_title: City of Ruston Parks and Recreation Reservations
cards.access_notes: Open adjoining park areas are public; a paid pavilion reservation is optional and applies only to the reserved facility.

cards.title: Walk Huckleberry Trails Park
cards.subtitle: Ruston city park
cards.notes: Make it a casual group walk or pause outdoors between classes; use the public park area without reserving a pavilion or buying anything.
cards.short_summary: A named city park for a free outdoor reset.
cards.evidence_claim: Ruston Parks and Recreation lists Huckleberry Trails Park and states that adjoining park areas remain open and available to the public at all times.
cards.source_title: City of Ruston Parks and Recreation Reservations
cards.access_notes: Public adjoining areas are available without a reservation; pavilion reservations are optional and priced separately.

cards.title: Hang out at Memorial Park
cards.subtitle: Ruston city park
cards.notes: Bring a friend for a quiet outdoor break in the public park area; Memorial Park is first-come, first-served and not reservable.
cards.short_summary: A named, first-come Ruston park for a no-cost outdoor hang.
cards.evidence_claim: Ruston Parks and Recreation lists Memorial Park as first-come, first-served and says adjoining city-park areas remain open and available to the public at all times.
cards.source_title: City of Ruston Parks and Recreation Reservations
cards.access_notes: Memorial Park is first-come, first-served and not reservable; follow city ordinances while using the public park.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Louisiana Tech study settings, from reservable-free library group rooms and research collections to discipline-specific collaborative spaces.

cards.title: Settle Into a Low-Stimulation Study Session
cards.subtitle: Main floor of Prescott Memorial Library
cards.notes: Bring headphones or a quiet assignment, then use the privacy chairs, adjustable lamps and charging outlets for a lower-stimulation work session.
cards.short_summary: An acoustically treated room with adaptable lighting, sensory tools and individual seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech reports that the main-floor Sensory Space is open to all Tech students and includes acoustic panels, adjustable lamps, privacy chairs and outlets.
cards.source_title: New Sensory Space opens in Prescott Memorial Library
cards.access_notes: Open to all Louisiana Tech students during Prescott Memorial Library operating hours; consult the current library-hours page before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Prescott Memorial Library Main-Floor Research Computers
cards.title: Start a Source-Heavy Assignment at the Research Computers
cards.subtitle: Second floor, designated as the library’s main floor
cards.notes: Use this area when an assignment needs library databases or catalog work; bring your Tech credentials for resources restricted to current affiliates.
cards.short_summary: A computer-equipped research area near the library’s principal service desks and reference collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The library’s current floor directory places research computers, the Reference Information Desk and the reference collection on Prescott’s main floor.
cards.access_notes: Use during library hours. Some databases require current Louisiana Tech credentials, while designated guest computers support on-site research.

cards.entity_name: Prescott Memorial Library Group Study Room 610
cards.title: Bring a Small Team to Room 610
cards.subtitle: Sixth floor of Prescott Memorial Library
cards.notes: Arrive with three to eight people and have one Tech student ready to leave a valid ID at circulation; the room cannot be reserved in advance.
cards.short_summary: A sixth-floor, first-come group room for collaborative academic work.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech identifies PML 610 as a group study room and states that rooms serve groups of three to eight, require student ID sign-in and cannot be reserved.
cards.access_notes: For groups of 3–8. A Tech student must sign in and leave a valid Tech ID at the Circulation Desk; first come, no reservations or stated time limit.

cards.entity_name: Prescott Memorial Library Group Study Room 710
cards.title: Work Through a Group Project in Room 710
cards.subtitle: Seventh floor of Prescott Memorial Library
cards.notes: Choose this room for discussion-based work with three to eight collaborators, then complete the required Tech ID sign-in at the circulation desk.
cards.short_summary: A seventh-floor collaboration room positioned among the library’s book collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The current floor directory lists PML 710 on the seventh floor, while the facilities policy defines library group-room eligibility and sign-in rules.
cards.access_notes: For groups of 3–8. A Tech student must leave a valid Tech ID at circulation; rooms are first come and unavailable for regular meetings or classes.

cards.entity_name: Prescott Memorial Library Group Study Room 810
cards.title: Take Collaborative Work Up to Room 810
cards.subtitle: Eighth floor of Prescott Memorial Library
cards.notes: Use Room 810 for a three-to-eight-person review session, presentation rehearsal or shared problem set after checking in at circulation with a Tech ID.
cards.short_summary: An eighth-floor group room suited to work that benefits from conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech’s current directory identifies PML 810 as the eighth-floor group study room; its facilities page sets a three-to-eight-person capacity.
cards.access_notes: For groups of 3–8. Check in at the Circulation Desk with a valid Tech ID; advance reservations are not accepted and no time limit is stated.

cards.entity_name: Prescott Memorial Library Third-Floor Periodicals Area
cards.title: Read Current and Bound Periodicals Near the Source
cards.subtitle: Third floor of Prescott Memorial Library
cards.notes: Head here when your topic depends on journals or newspapers, and ask the floor’s information desk about locating or using periodical material.
cards.short_summary: A collection-centered workspace with periodicals, newspapers and a dedicated information desk.
cards.evidence_claim: The library’s current floor directory places periodicals, newspapers and the Periodicals Information Desk on Prescott Memorial Library’s third floor.
cards.access_notes: Enter during Prescott Memorial Library hours. Periodical borrowing varies by format and affiliation; consult staff before removing material from the floor.

cards.title: Build a Primary-Source Session Around the Archives
cards.subtitle: Fourth floor of Prescott Memorial Library
cards.notes: Request materials before arriving, carry photo ID and plan to take notes in pencil; bags, food and drinks must remain outside the reading workspace.
cards.short_summary: A supervised reading room for university archives, manuscripts and rare regional materials.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech requires Special Collections materials to be consulted in the fourth-floor reading room and recommends appointments because access may be limited.
cards.access_notes: Appointment recommended; walk-ins may face restrictions. Bring picture ID. Current hours are Monday–Thursday 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m. and Friday 8 a.m.–noon.

cards.title: Choose a Quiet Nook or Balcony in the Business Building
cards.subtitle: Across three floors of the College of Business
cards.notes: Walk the three floors to match the task to a setting: use a quiet niche for solo reading or a collaborative area when conversation is necessary.
cards.short_summary: A mix of quiet niches, balconies and collaborative areas inside the business building.
cards.evidence_claim: The College of Business says its three floors contain collaborative learning spaces, balconies, quiet study nooks, six breakout rooms and 24/7 student access.
cards.access_notes: The college states that students have 24/7 building access. Room-specific availability or reservation rules are not published on the cited page.

cards.entity_name: Integrated Engineering and Science Building Dynamic Learning Areas
cards.title: Spread Out for Technical Work in IESB
cards.subtitle: Integrated Engineering and Science Building
cards.notes: Bring project notes or a collaborative problem set and use the building’s dynamic learning areas; eligible students should carry their campus ID for entry.
cards.short_summary: Flexible learning areas designed around engineering and science coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech identifies dynamic learning areas inside IESB, and its current access policy grants College of Engineering and Science students card access.
cards.access_notes: College of Engineering and Science students receive campus-ID access, including 24/7 access except during University closures; access is major-based and assigned quarterly.

cards.entity_name: Robinson B Residential Suites Study Rooms
cards.title: Keep Resident Study Sessions Close to Home
cards.subtitle: Private and group rooms in Robinson B Residential Suites
cards.notes: If you live in Robinson B, use the private room for focused work or move a collaborative assignment into one of the residence’s group study rooms.
cards.short_summary: Resident-only private and group study rooms within an entrepreneurship living-learning community.
cards.evidence_claim: The College of Business lists private and group study rooms among the amenities in Robinson B Residential Suites for Entrepreneurship LLC residents.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to residents and authorized guests under housing rules; the cited page does not publish room hours or reservation procedures.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on practical corridors between Louisiana Tech and central Ruston, each paired with one directly sourced reason to stop.

cards.title: Catch Downtown Activity at Railroad Park
cards.subtitle: West Park Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Check the city calendar, then use this downtown park as a starting point for nearby shops, eateries, concerts, or community events.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor downtown venue surrounded by shops and places to eat.
cards.evidence_claim: Railroad Park at 101 W. Park Avenue is a downtown city park hosting concerts, festivals, speaking engagements, pet shows, and other events.
cards.access_notes: Located at 101 W. Park Ave.; event access and schedules vary, so check the current calendar before visiting.

cards.title: Browse Clothing and Gifts at The Fashion
cards.subtitle: West Park Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Step inside the downtown storefront to browse clothing, shoes, jewelry, bags, and gifts; purchasing merchandise is optional.
cards.short_summary: A locally owned downtown shop with apparel and gift selections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fashion of Ruston at 208 W. Park Avenue sells clothing, gifts, jewelry, shoes, bags, and related merchandise.
cards.source_title: The Fashion of Ruston | Experience Ruston
cards.access_notes: The listed storefront is 208 W. Park Ave.; consult the business's current channels before relying on operating hours.

cards.title: Pause for Coffee Beside the Tracks
cards.subtitle: West Railroad Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the seating for a study break or conversation, and review the current menu before ordering coffee or a treat.
cards.short_summary: A coffeehouse near downtown with seating suited to studying or meeting.
cards.evidence_claim: The Depot Coffee House at 211 W. Railroad Avenue offers coffee and treats in a space described for studying and meeting.
cards.source_title: The Depot Coffee House | Experience Ruston
cards.access_notes: Located at 211 W. Railroad Ave.; verify current hours and menu with the business before making a dedicated trip.

cards.title: See Work by Ruston Artists
cards.subtitle: North Trenton Street corridor
cards.notes: Browse the marketplace's local art and handmade work, then ask whether its nearby gallery has a current show or workshop.
cards.short_summary: A downtown marketplace centered on work from local artists and artisans.
cards.evidence_claim: Creative Exchange at 301 N. Trenton Street features work by local artists and artisans and operates an associated gallery at 112 W. Alabama Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Marketplace address is 301 N. Trenton St.; gallery programming is periodic, so confirm exhibits or workshops in advance.

cards.title: Read the Parish Through Its Artifacts
cards.subtitle: North Vienna Street corridor
cards.notes: Look for the period furnishings, photographs, clothing, and seven Walls That Talk murals inside the 1886 Kidd-Davis home.
cards.short_summary: A historic house museum interpreting Lincoln Parish through objects and murals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lincoln Parish Museum at 609 N. Vienna Street occupies the 1886 Kidd-Davis home and displays period artifacts plus seven history murals with recorded stories.
cards.access_notes: Located at 609 N. Vienna St.; confirm public opening times and any admission requirements before visiting.

cards.title: Check the Historic Dixie Stage
cards.subtitle: North Vienna Street corridor
cards.notes: Review the performance calendar before walking over; community theater, concerts, and other programmed events use this restored venue.
cards.short_summary: A restored downtown theater hosting varied arts programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dixie Center for the Arts at 212 N. Vienna Street reopened after restoration in 2006 and presents programming with local theater and arts partners.
cards.source_title: Dixie Center for the Arts | Experience Ruston
cards.access_notes: Located at 212 N. Vienna St.; entry depends on the scheduled event, and advance tickets may be required.

cards.title: Watch Pollinators from the Gazebo
cards.subtitle: North Vienna Street and West Georgia Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Pause at the gazebo and observe the flowering plants for visiting butterflies without disturbing the garden or its pollinators.
cards.short_summary: A planted downtown garden designed to attract butterflies.
cards.evidence_claim: The Butterfly Garden at N. Vienna Street and W. Georgia Avenue contains pollinator-attracting plants and a gazebo for viewing butterflies.
cards.access_notes: Located at the corner of N. Vienna St. and W. Georgia Ave.; no operating schedule is stated on the source page.

cards.title: Meet Local Producers Saturday Morning
cards.subtitle: East Mississippi Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Visit during the listed Saturday session to browse seasonal produce and handmade goods while seeing the facility's exterior mural.
cards.short_summary: A weekly covered market pairing local products with music and demonstrations.
cards.evidence_claim: Ruston Farmers Market at 220 E. Mississippi Avenue offers local food and handmade goods, live music, demonstrations, and Saturday hours from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.
cards.access_notes: The source currently lists Saturdays from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. at 220 E. Mississippi Ave.; check for seasonal or event changes.

cards.title: Spot a Downtown Event Backdrop
cards.subtitle: West Mississippi Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Look over the building's rustic-modern exterior while passing, or contact the venue directly before planning a private event.
cards.short_summary: A photogenic downtown event venue in a restored commercial setting.
cards.evidence_claim: The Norton Building at 207 W. Mississippi Avenue is a downtown venue used for weddings, receptions, parties, and other events.
cards.access_notes: Located at 207 W. Mississippi Ave.; interior access is event-dependent and should be arranged with the venue.

cards.title: Take a Daylight Picnic Break
cards.subtitle: East Mississippi Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Bring a daytime picnic and use the wooded setting, pavilion, or outdoor tables; plan to leave before the posted dusk closing.
cards.short_summary: A wooded neighborhood park equipped for outdoor picnics.
cards.evidence_claim: Roberts Park at 1000 E. Mississippi Avenue is a wooded park with picnic areas and a pavilion, listed as open from dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: The published hours are dawn to dusk at 1000 E. Mississippi Ave.; pavilion use may have separate requirements.

warnings: Coordinates and maps URLs are null because exact values were not independently verified from direct map records.
Several destination pages are maintained by the Ruston Lincoln Convention and Visitors Bureau; source_kind is classified as government.
Purchase-required marks commercial transactions or ticketed programming, not a claim that merely viewing an exterior requires payment.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From medallions dropped into a fountain to class rings spending the night in a clock tower, these documented rituals mark arrivals, milestones, and homecomings at Louisiana Tech.

cards.title: Drop a Tenet Medallion into the Mist
cards.subtitle: Freshman Convocation at the Lady of the Mist
cards.notes: At Freshman Convocation, watch new Bulldogs place their Tenet Medallions in the fountain as a symbol of investing in their studies.
cards.short_summary: A first-year keepsake begins its story underwater in the Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech documents that first-year students drop Tenet Medallions into the Lady of the Mist during Freshman Convocation.
cards.source_title: Student volunteers encourage giving through Student Advancement Team
cards.access_notes: The documented ritual occurs during Freshman Convocation and is intended for incoming students; others may observe only when invited.

cards.title: Walk Between Two Lines of Tech Blue
cards.subtitle: The Quad route to the Lady of the Mist
cards.notes: Join the incoming class route through the Quad while alumni dressed in Tech Blue form a welcoming passage toward the fountain.
cards.short_summary: Alumni turn a campus walkway into a blue-clad welcome line.
cards.evidence_claim: The Louisiana Tech Alumni Association says alumni line the Quad walkways in Tech Blue, creating a passage for freshmen walking to the Lady of the Mist.
cards.access_notes: Participation is tied to Freshman Convocation; alumni should follow the Alumni Association’s event instructions.

cards.entity_name: Lady of the Mist Welcome and Farewell
cards.title: Let the Lady Welcome You—and Bid You Farewell
cards.subtitle: A 1938 Alma Mater figure in the Quad
cards.notes: Read the fountain inscription and frame a photo around the figure that symbolically greets new students and sends graduates onward.
cards.short_summary: One sculpture performs both the campus hello and goodbye.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech states that the Lady of the Mist symbolizes Alma Mater welcoming new students and bidding farewell to graduates.
cards.access_notes: The sculpture stands in the campus Quad; remain outside the fountain and follow posted campus-access rules.

cards.title: Escort Class Rings Down Alumni Walkway
cards.subtitle: The opening movement of Louisiana Tech’s Ring Tradition
cards.notes: Follow the ceremonial route as official class rings travel along Alumni Walkway to the brick honoring first graduate Harry Howard.
cards.short_summary: Before reaching their owners, the rings retrace Tech history on foot.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech’s alumni magazine documents a Procession of the Rings in which official rings travel down Alumni Walkway to Harry Howard’s brick.
cards.access_notes: This is a scheduled ceremonial event; confirm the current procession date and spectator arrangements with Alumni Engagement.

cards.title: Leave the Rings in the Clock Tower Overnight
cards.subtitle: An overnight pause before the Ring Ceremony
cards.notes: See the procession deliver official rings to Centennial Clock Tower, where they rest overnight before the next morning’s presentation.
cards.short_summary: Louisiana Tech’s class rings spend a ceremonial night under the clock.
cards.evidence_claim: The University’s account of the Ring Tradition says processed class rings rest overnight in Centennial Clock Tower before the Ring Ceremony.
cards.access_notes: The overnight placement is ceremonial, not an invitation to enter the tower; observe only from authorized public areas.

cards.title: Choose One Tenet to Carry Inside Your Ring
cards.subtitle: A personalized inscription in the Official Class Ring
cards.notes: At the Ring Ceremony, look inside each recipient’s ring for the chosen Tenet of Tech engraved beside the owner’s name and bullmark.
cards.short_summary: Each class ring hides one personally selected Tech principle.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech reports that Official Ring recipients choose one Tenet of Tech for engraving inside the ring and receive rings individually at the Ring Ceremony.
cards.access_notes: Ring eligibility and ceremony participation are administered by Alumni Engagement; purchasing an official ring is required for recipients.

cards.title: Cross the Stage, Then Collect Twelve Tenets
cards.subtitle: The graduation-side medallion ritual
cards.notes: After crossing the commencement stage, collect the commemorative medallion from your dean and inspect its ring of twelve Tenets.
cards.short_summary: Graduation ends with the University’s principles pressed into metal.
cards.evidence_claim: Current graduate guidelines state that graduates receive a commemorative medallion from their dean after crossing the stage; the Spring 2025 program says it bears the 12 Tenets.
cards.access_notes: The medallion presentation is part of commencement and limited to participating graduates after they cross the stage.

cards.title: Meet the Twenty-Second Bulldog in the Line
cards.subtitle: Tech XXII, affectionately called Techie
cards.notes: Look for Tech XXII at an authorized campus appearance and photograph the current live mascot without crowding or handling him uninvited.
cards.short_summary: The mascot is a living bulldog with a Roman numeral and family lineage.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech’s official 2026 podcast identifies Tech XXII as the current bulldog mascot, notes that Tech XXI was his father, and says he was introduced in 2018.
cards.access_notes: Meet Tech XXII only at announced appearances; follow the handler’s directions and do not feed or touch the dog without permission.

cards.title: Tell the Bulldog Story in Red and Blue
cards.subtitle: A campus legend traced to fall 1899
cards.notes: Read the University’s account beside a Bulldog landmark, noting that the alleged grave site and the students’ identities remain unknown.
cards.short_summary: Tech’s mascot and colors share one heroic but unverifiable origin story.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech recounts a legend that students buried a heroic bulldog wrapped in red and blue, later choosing Bulldogs and those colors; the University notes key details remain unknown.
cards.access_notes: Treat this as a University-documented legend, not verified history; do not search for or disturb any alleged burial site.

cards.title: Mark a Century of Homecoming with the Parade
cards.subtitle: The campus procession during Homecoming Week
cards.notes: Choose a public viewing spot along the announced campus route, arrive before the procession, and leave roadways clear for participants.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming’s moving centerpiece crossed campus for its centennial year.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech’s official 2025 Homecoming page celebrated 100 years of Homecoming and listed a campus Homecoming Parade among the featured events.
cards.access_notes: The parade occurs only during scheduled Homecoming programming; consult the current official schedule and route before attending.

warnings: The University explicitly presents the Bulldog origin as a legend and acknowledges that the burial location and students’ identities are unknown.
The Ring Tradition source dates to 2018; current ceremony dates, eligibility, and viewing arrangements should be reconfirmed with Alumni Engagement.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Louisiana Tech University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A conservative Friday-to-Sunday sequence linking campus orientation landmarks, student recreation, downtown Ruston, and a Sunday library reset.

cards.title: Friday Arrival at Hale Hall
cards.subtitle: Stop 1 · Use the admissions landmark to get oriented
cards.notes: Start at Hale Hall, identify Railroad Avenue and the Quad on the current campus map, then continue on foot toward the campus core.
cards.short_summary: Establish a reliable campus reference point before the weekend begins.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech identifies Hale Hall as the first brick building on Railroad Avenue and places the Office of Admissions on its first floor.
cards.access_notes: Visitor parking is listed in front of Hale Hall; campus parking elsewhere requires a permit.

cards.title: Meet the Lady of the Mist
cards.subtitle: Stop 2 · Learn the landmark at the center of the Quad
cards.notes: Walk into the Quad, locate the fountain sculpture, and read the university’s account of what the Lady symbolizes for students and graduates.
cards.short_summary: Connect the campus layout with one documented Louisiana Tech tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech describes the Lady of the Mist as a sculpture in a fountain in the quadrangle that symbolizes Alma Mater welcoming students and bidding graduates farewell.
cards.access_notes: The sculpture is outdoors in the Quad; fountain operation and temporary restrictions are not guaranteed.

cards.title: Friday Dinner at Tech Table
cards.subtitle: Stop 3 · Learn how the main residential dining hall works
cards.notes: Use a meal swipe or confirm another payment option before entering, then note the True Balance station if food-allergen needs apply.
cards.short_summary: Turn the first meal into a practical introduction to campus dining.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech identifies Tech Table as an all-you-care-to-eat residential dining hall and says meal swipes are accepted there.
cards.access_notes: Check the linked dining-hours service before visiting; a meal plan, buddy swipe, declining balance, or other payment may be required.

cards.title: Friday-Night Bowling at Lambright
cards.subtitle: Stop 4 · End the evening on the six campus lanes
cards.notes: Bring a valid student ID, check in before the Friday closing time, and ask the desk whether reservations have limited lane availability.
cards.short_summary: Choose a structured, under-21 evening activity on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lambright bowling alley has six lanes and automatic scoring and is free for currently enrolled Louisiana Tech students with valid ID.
cards.access_notes: Friday hours are 9 a.m.–10 p.m. A valid student or member ID is required; facility areas may be unavailable for reservations.

cards.title: Saturday Climb at Lambright
cards.subtitle: Stop 5 · Try the recreation center’s belay-equipped wall
cards.notes: Arrive during the Saturday climbing window, wear closed-toe shoes, and follow staff instructions before using an auto-belay route.
cards.short_summary: Begin Saturday with a supervised indoor recreation option.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech states that the Lambright rock wall is 29.5 feet tall with two manual belays and six auto-belays.
cards.access_notes: Saturday rock-wall hours are noon–4 p.m. Valid student or member ID is required; current students use Lambright free.

cards.title: Walk Hideaway Park
cards.subtitle: Stop 6 · Follow the trail beside the seven-acre lake
cards.notes: Visit during daylight, choose the walking trail or disc-golf course, and avoid entering reserved pavilions or the ropes course uninvited.
cards.short_summary: Shift outdoors for a flexible campus-park break.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech says Hideaway Park is open daily during daylight and contains a hilly trail, pavilions, an 18-hole disc-golf course, and a seven-acre lake.
cards.access_notes: Open every day during daylight hours. The low-ropes course requires group scheduling; pavilion reservations may affect availability.

cards.title: Explore Downtown from Railroad Park
cards.subtitle: Stop 7 · Use the city park as a downtown waypoint
cards.notes: Start at the park’s West Park Avenue address, scan posted event notices, and keep any shopping or dining choices optional.
cards.short_summary: Add a simple downtown Ruston stop without depending on a scheduled event.
cards.evidence_claim: Experience Ruston lists Railroad Park at 101 W. Park Ave. and describes it as a city park and downtown event venue near shops and eateries.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public venue; check posted notices because concerts, festivals, and other events can change access conditions.

cards.title: Saturday Photo at Centennial Plaza
cards.subtitle: Stop 8 · Re-enter campus through a mapped landmark
cards.notes: Locate the plaza and tower on the current campus map, pause for an exterior photo, and use the landmark to trace your route back east.
cards.short_summary: Practice navigating campus with a visually distinct mapped destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech’s July 2025 campus map identifies Centennial Plaza/Centennial Tower as campus landmark number 12.
cards.source_title: Louisiana Tech University Campus Map — July 2025
cards.access_notes: Plan this as an exterior stop; temporary event restrictions and interior tower access are not established by the map.

cards.entity_name: F. Jay Taylor Visual Arts Center
cards.title: Find the Visual Arts Center
cards.subtitle: Stop 9 · Add an arts landmark to your campus map
cards.notes: Walk to the named arts center, photograph the exterior, and check building postings before attempting to enter any gallery or studio.
cards.short_summary: Round out the campus tour with a clearly mapped arts destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech’s July 2025 campus map identifies the F. Jay Taylor Visual Arts Center as campus destination number 22.
cards.source_title: Louisiana Tech University Campus Map — July 2025
cards.access_notes: Treat this as an exterior wayfinding stop unless current gallery or building access is posted on site.

cards.title: Sunday Reset at Prescott Library
cards.subtitle: Stop 10 · Close the weekend by preparing for Monday
cards.notes: Bring your class list, find one dependable study area, and use the visit to identify where library help and research tools are located.
cards.short_summary: Finish with a practical study-space orientation before classes resume.
cards.evidence_claim: Louisiana Tech publishes fall, winter, and spring Sunday hours of 2–11 p.m. for Prescott Memorial Library.
cards.access_notes: Fall, winter, and spring Sunday hours are 2–11 p.m.; summer Sunday hours are 5–9 p.m. Holiday and quarter-break hours can differ.
